chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Anbasa al-A'bid who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: If you do not have natural weeping, then force yourself to weep.

key_terms.الْعَابِدِ: The worshipper (epithet of the narrator Anbasa)
key_terms.فَتَبَكَّ: Then make yourself cry / force weeping

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they cannot naturally cry during prayer or supplication?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises that if a person does not naturally feel the emotion of weeping during supplication or Quran recitation, they should actively force themselves to cry. This highlights the importance of emotional engagement and humility in acts of worship. In Shia tradition, this 'forced' tears (bukaa') are seen as a means to awaken the heart (qalb) and bridge the gap between outward ritual and inward spiritual presence (hudhur al-qalb).

en.ammaar-muslim: [1/1548] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Anbasa al-A’bid who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: If you are not one who can cry outrightly (i.e. when reciting the Qur’an and in supplication) then make like you are crying (i.e. force yourself)
